headline: High-risk shared filesystem and server-side execution in n8n can leak or corrupt workflow data; nuwa-skill adds limited direct conflict but no documented isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute workflow nodes that may consume content as trusted input; if nuwa-skill feeds attacker-controlled text into n8n workflows, prompt injection is plausible. nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted egress and no input surfaces are documented, so the bridge is inferred rather than proven, which keeps this below high.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill output is copied into an n8n AI Agent node or file-backed workflow step
IF n8n workflow logic treats file or message content as instructions without validation
mitigations: Add a fixed allowlist prompt wrapper in n8n
Insert a human review step before any tool-using node
Strip instructions from imported text before passing it onward
Use separate workspaces for raw inputs and executable prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n explicitly touches the server filesystem and handles per-credential secrets, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress. If both operate on the same workflow data, sensitive content can move from n8n into nuwa-skill outputs or external calls. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents process the same sensitive workflow payload
IF n8n passes file contents or secrets into nuwa-skill-triggered requests
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared payloads
Store credentials only in n8n credential vault
Redact files before external transmission
Limit nuwa-skill to non-sensitive datasets
requires-engineering: add field-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and broad egress; nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. Even without explicit write access in nuwa-skill, both can act on shared mutable workflow state through connected systems, creating contention or overwrites. Because nuwa-skill write surfaces are undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream system or datastore
IF n8n workflows and nuwa-skill jobs target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Add optimistic locking on shared records
Disable concurrent runs on the same dataset
requires-engineering: implement cross-agent lease locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate tools, so its outputs may be treated as actionable workflow inputs. nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent with no documented verification barrier, so if n8n forwards its own generated content into nuwa-skill, errors can cascade across steps. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF n8n output is consumed by nuwa-skill without a verification step
IF either agent is allowed to trigger downstream actions from unreviewed text
mitigations: Require explicit validation between steps
Add schema checks on all handoffs
Log and diff intermediate outputs
Block action-taking nodes from unverified content
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention fields are documented for nuwa-skill, while n8n handles per-credential secrets and whatever the workflow processes. That makes a concrete compliance mismatch unproven; the only documented issue is that n8n may process regulated data if the workflow does. Because the other agent’s compliance posture is absent, uncertainty limits this to low.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated data such as EU PII or PHI
IF nuwa-skill is used in a jurisdiction or policy regime requiring documented residency or retention controls
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Document retention for each integration
Use separate tenants for sensitive jobs
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
